summary.headline: Electronics Mart Q4 FY26 revenue rose 15% to INR1,913 crores and SSSG hit 12.2%, with EBITDA margin up to 6.7%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 15% YoY to INR1,913 crores, with EBITDA up 20% to INR129 crores and margin expanding to 6.7% from 5.6%. Same-store sales growth was 12.2% in the quarter, helped by GST rate cuts, festive demand and mobile launches, while FY26 SSSG was 5.3%. FY26 revenue rose 7% to INR7,183 crores with EBITDA of INR438 crores (6.1% margin) and PAT of INR107 crores. Management said working capital requirements have fallen and pre Ind AS operating cash flow reached INR299 crores for the year.

segments.name: South cluster (AP, Telangana, Hyderabad)
segments.commentary: Management cites a 6.5% EBITDA margin for the South cluster, with about INR6,000-6,500 crores of revenue from the region (69 AP stores, 46 Telangana, 72 Hyderabad city). Hyderabad city generated about INR4,122 crores in FY26; Hyderabad SSSG was double-digit in Q4.

segments.name: North cluster (NCR/Delhi)
segments.commentary: Delhi NCR operates 35 stores with about INR590 crores of revenue in FY26 and is now EBITDA positive on a full-year basis. Management guided to 25-30% growth in FY27 and a 2.5-3% EBITDA margin, versus about 0.2-0.3% now; Q4 Delhi like-to-like sales were reported at about 19%.

segments.name: Mature vs new stores
segments.commentary: Of 223 stores, 83 are over 4 years old (about 7.3% EBITDA margin) and 140 are under 4 years old (about 3.1% margin).

segments.name: Product categories
segments.commentary: Panels grew 13% and mobile phones 28% in Q4; washing machines grew strongly in double digits, refrigerators were stable, and large appliance mix fell from 47% to 42%.

guidance_outlook: Organic store additions of about 20 in FY27 (12-15 in NCR and AP/Telangana per management, plus Delhi and South openings), with capex of about INR3-4 crores per store assumed for 8,000-10,000 sq ft stores.
New East entry starting with 5-7 stores in Kolkata by end-Q2 or start-Q3 FY27; FY27 real estate spend of about INR50 crores, up to INR100 crores over 12-14 months.

NCR revenue target of INR800+ crores in FY27 (vs INR585 crores in FY26), with 2-4% EBITDA margin; Andhra Pradesh (INR1,100+ crores) and Telangana (INR1,000 crores) expected to deliver higher single-digit SSSG.
North cluster margin to be 3-4% higher than now by FY28 (not stated as an exact level).
Management expects ASPs up at least 5-6% on average in FY26 with volume held; price hikes are passed through to customers; inventory to be bought 2-3% higher at newer prices for the next 20 days.
capex_capacity: Store count 223 (83 over 4 years old, 140 under 4 years); Q4 added 4 stores (NCR, Telangana, 2 in Andhra Pradesh).
Management plans 12-15 organic stores in NCR, AP and Telangana, with 4-5 Delhi stores getting ready, and 7-8 more stores in NCR; new Kolkata cluster to start with 5-7 stores by end-Q2 or start-Q3.
Store size 8,000-10,000 sq ft typical, capex about INR3-4 crores per store, similar product mix in new regions.
Working capital requirement reduced; cash flow prioritised over expansion, with loans against property repaid organically.
Franchise model not in use; all stores company-operated, with franchising only to be explored if OEMs support it.
demand_pricing: Q4 demand robust across categories; washing machines grew strongly in double digits, panels 13%, mobile phones 28% (new launches in January and March).
ASPs rose at least 5-6% on average in FY26 for the same volume (bigger TV sizes after GST cut, higher-star ACs), and management says no category saw ASP decline.
Price hikes on RAC products of about INR1,500-2,000 per SKU are passed on to customers; additional inventory bought at 2-3% higher prices.
Entry-level mobile price hikes (below INR20,000) have limited impact, as the company's mobile ASP is about INR35,000-40,000.
Sourcing is essentially direct from OEMs/brands; distributor purchases are about INR50 crores a year, with margins unchanged.
Competition: NCR faces Croma, Reliance and Vijay Sales; South competes mostly with mom-and-pop stores, which drives the margin gap.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Hyderabad SSSG double-digit in Q4 and how should FY27 be read?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to the GST cut benefit across categories (TVs, washing machines, dishwashers, refrigerators, cooling products) plus mobile launches; early Q1 trends were good.

qa_highlights.question: How did gross margin hold up as large appliance mix fell from 47% to 42%?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins were supported by higher-margin categories (mobile accessories, built-in appliances, audio) and better throughput; management expects margins to hold or improve.

qa_highlights.question: Store opening cadence and cash flow deployment?
qa_highlights.answer: Store openings slowed as Delhi was a new market in FY25; Hyderabad adds only 1-2 stores a year. Management said cash is reinvested, working capital has fallen and loans are repaid organically.

qa_highlights.question: Delhi/NCR margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: Targets INR800+ crores revenue and 2-4% EBITDA margin in FY27, with a 3-4% higher margin than now by FY28; the NCR cluster is EBITDA positive for the full year.

qa_highlights.question: Franchise model?
qa_highlights.answer: No franchising currently; management said it would consider franchising only in a region where OEM support and partner alignment exist, citing seasonality and consumer experience.

qa_highlights.question: Why enter Kolkata while NCR is still stabilising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Delhi stabilisation is done and growth will be organic; Kolkata is a new cluster with a 12-14 month learning cycle, starting with 5-7 stores by end-Q2 or start-Q3.

risks_watch: Delhi/NCR execution: Q4 growth was off a low base, and management targets 25-30% growth and a 2.5-3% margin in FY27 from a 0.2-0.3% base.
Summer and cooling demand: Delhi started late, and about 50% of Q1 remained at the time of the call; cooling products are key to the quarter's margin.
Store maturity: 140 stores under 4 years old run at 3.1% margin versus 7.3% for mature stores.
Working capital and inventory: inventory days were 73 at 31 March 2026; RAC inventory was bought at older prices, with more purchases at higher prices expected.
Kolkata entry is new and capital-intensive (up to INR100 crores of real estate over 12-14 months).
summary.management_tone: Confident on South/Hyderabad and the margin trajectory, but more measured on Delhi, where management said growth will be more organic. Some answers were evasive on volume-versus-value splits and on Q1 trends.
key_quotes: We also saw a meaningful operating leverage coming through, resulting in an improvement in our operating margins, even as we continue to add new stores to our network.
Mature stores continue to demonstrate strong performance with an EBITDA margin of approximately 7.3%, while newer stores are currently operating at 3.1%, consistent with their stage of ramp-up.
So Calcutta would be a new base for East.

growth.why: FY27 guidance centres on NCR revenue of INR800+ crore (25-30% growth) at 2-4% EBITDA margin and ~20 organic stores plus a Kolkata entry (5-7 stores by end-Q2/start-Q3, ~INR50 crore real estate); backing is partly specific (store count, capex per store, NCR target) but no firm order or utilisation data, and the 20 store adds are a cut from earlier plans.
